queries: information and cooperation in common pool resource games

title: Disorderly Discourse: Analyzing the Internal Disunity of Russia’s Liberal Opposition
gloss: Asks why Russia's liberal opposition to Putin fails to unify, especially after the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, comparing Alexei Navalny, Mikhail Khodorkovsky, Garry Kasparov and Maxim Katz. Weighs ideological, tactical and personality differences, and considers the aftermath of Navalny's death.
queries: why the Russian opposition is divided

title: Investigating the Effects of Populist Rhetoric on Confidence in Representative Democracy in the United States
gloss: Tests whether exposure to populist, anti-establishment rhetoric reduces Americans' confidence in representative democratic institutions, using a survey experiment that shows participants neutral or populist messaging from a presidential candidate.
queries: does populist rhetoric reduce trust in democracy

title: The Birds, The Bees, and The Bureaucracy: A Cross-National Analysis of Abortion Policy Determinants
gloss: Explains why abortion laws range from total bans to abortion on demand across 187 countries, correlating abortion policy with development, gender equality, women's political representation, suffrage timing, education, labor force participation, income and religiosity. Bears on global reproductive health and gender equality.
queries: why abortion laws differ between countries
gender equality and liberal abortion laws

title: Corporate America Under Siege: The Electoral Effects of Political Attacks on Private Enterprise
gloss: Tests through an experiment whether voters reward politicians who publicly attack and punish corporations that take political stances, a tactic seen in fights like Florida's clash with Disney. Examines how partisanship and the harshness of the attack shape voter support.
queries: do voters support politicians attacking corporations
survey experiment on political rhetoric toward firms

title: How the Presence of Syrian Refugees Affects Elections in Turkey
gloss: Asks how the presence of Syrian refugees affected Turkey's 2023 presidential and parliamentary elections, where anti-refugee sentiment dominated campaigns. Combines provincial voting data, surveys and GIS analysis, and tests intergroup contact theory.
queries: effect of Syrian refugees on Turkish elections

title: War and Politics After Fifty Years: the Vietnam War and Vietnamese American Political Preferences on Immigration
gloss: Explores how the Vietnam War, refugee flight and resettlement shape Vietnamese Americans' relatively conservative views on immigration, and how those views differ by immigrant generation, age and nativity. Based mainly on qualitative interviews.
queries: Vietnam War legacy and immigration views

title: Correcting Republican Misperceptions of a Socialist Threat
gloss: Asks whether Republicans' belief that socialism is anti-democratic and popular among Democrats fuels their own anti-democratic attitudes, and whether correcting misperceptions with real data reduces that sentiment. Uses a survey of 720 partisans and a preregistered experiment with 1,396 Republicans.
queries: Republican fears of socialism and democracy
does correcting misperceptions reduce anti-democratic views

title: Machine Learning Analysis of COVID-19: Exploring Determinants of Spread, Mortality, and Governance Responses
gloss: Applies machine learning (LASSO regression and random forests with imputation) to 1,685 candidate variables across 172 countries to find the predictors of COVID-19 spread, mortality and effective government responses. Offers an inductive roadmap for variable selection in cross-national research and new hypotheses about governance.

acronyms.LASSO: least absolute shrinkage and selection operator

queries: what predicted COVID-19 death rates across countries
LASSO and random forest variable selection
inductive machine learning for social science

title: Coercion in the commons: Private university administrations’ responses to graduate worker unionization 2016-2025
gloss: Documents how private university administrations at Columbia, Harvard, Northwestern, Duke and Princeton responded to graduate worker union campaigns from 2016 to 2025. Using interviews with organizers, NLRB records and news, it codes tactics such as delaying bargaining, limiting the bargaining unit, anti-union messaging and hiring union-avoidance law firms.
queries: how universities fight graduate student unions
union busting tactics in higher education

title: Coercion or Cooperation: American Security Force Assistance in an Era of Great Power Competition
gloss: Examines how US security force assistance (SFA) must change as focus shifts from counterinsurgency to great power competition, comparing Ukraine, Taiwan and South Korea. Asks how attitudes toward military sovereignty, threat proximity, history with the US and economic integration affect a partner's embrace of American assistance.
queries: US military assistance to Ukraine Taiwan South Korea
security force assistance in great power competition
how partner nations accept US military aid
shift from counterinsurgency to deterring China and Russia

title: Meaningless Buzzword or Moral Call to Action? The Effect of the Term Genocide on Ukrainians’ Levels of Political Engagement Explored through Ethnic Identification
gloss: Uses a survey experiment to test whether calling Russia's war on Ukraine a genocide, rather than a war, increases political engagement and changes policy priorities among ethnic Ukrainians born in Ukraine and in the United States, and how it affects ethnic identification.
queries: does calling something genocide increase public action
Russia's war in Ukraine genocide debate
language of atrocity and foreign policy support

title: Shaping Success or Stifling Potential? Examining The Relationship Between Academic Achievement and Exclusionary Discipline in Chicago Public and Charter Schools
gloss: Asks whether Chicago charter schools use exclusionary discipline such as suspensions and expulsions disproportionately compared with public schools, and whether discipline rates relate to SAT scores, graduation and college enrollment.
queries: do charter schools suspend more students
Chicago charter schools versus public schools

title: Race-ing for Success A Mixed-Methods Analysis of Racial Inequality in NCAA DI Women’s Cross Country Running
gloss: Examines the underrepresentation of non-white American women in NCAA Division I women's cross country, where programs recruit international talent rather than developing domestic runners of color. Analyzes top-ten championship finishers from 2015 to 2024 and surveys Big Ten athletes, within a Critical Race Theory framework.
queries: racial diversity in college cross country
why few Black American women run distance in NCAA
race and gender in college sports

title: Navigating the Information Age: How a Saturated Media Environment Affects Political Knowledge
gloss: Tests experimentally whether having more news sources available helps or hinders how much people learn about a political topic in a short time, addressing fears of information overload in today's high-choice media environment of cable news, the internet and social media. Also checks whether effects differ by education and political interest. Advised by Mary McGrath.
queries: does more news make people better informed
experiment on number of news sources and learning
how the internet and social media affect what voters know

title: "We are the union”: a case study of a local union's internal structure
gloss: Case study of the internal structure of a local labor union, likely how its organization, leadership and member participation shape union democracy and the idea that members themselves are the union.
queries: how local unions are organized internally

title: Manipulated Maps, Manipulated Participation: How Partisan Gerrymandering Influences Conventional and Unconventional Political Engagement
gloss: Asks how partisan gerrymandering affects Americans' conventional participation (voting, contacting officials) and unconventional participation (protest), using Cooperative Election Study data and a survey experiment that primes people to think about gerrymandering in their district.
queries: effects of redistricting on political engagement

title: Protest Participation Through the Lens of Grievance Theory: How Economic Factors and Individuals’ Perceptions of Conditions Shape Significant Anti-Government Protests From 2017 to 2023
gloss: Tests grievance theory by asking whether objective economic conditions or individuals' perceptions of economic hardship better explain participation in major anti-government protests worldwide from 2017 to 2023. Combines cross-national macroeconomic indicators with survey measures of relative deprivation, financial insecurity and government accountability.

title: Reducing Affective Polarization: Is Proportional Representation the Answer?
gloss: Tests whether proportional representation electoral systems causally reduce affective polarization, using difference-in-differences with Mahalanobis distance matching rather than the OLS used in earlier comparative work. Also probes mechanisms such as economic inequality, representation of disadvantaged groups and satisfaction with democracy.
queries: electoral system reform and affective polarization
PR versus first past the post
can changing elections reduce partisan hostility

title: From Expansion to Equity: Leveraging Telehealth to Mitigate Healthcare Disparities During and Beyond the COVID-19 Pandemic
gloss: Compares how the COVID-19 telehealth expansion affected healthcare access, patient engagement and public trust in South Korea's centralized system and the decentralized US system, with attention to older and rural patients facing digital literacy, broadband and regulatory barriers.
queries: telehealth for rural and elderly patients
future of telemedicine after the pandemic

title: Austerity and the Economic Gender Gap
gloss: Asks whether austerity and fiscal consolidation disproportionately hurt women economically, using time-series cross-section regressions of fiscal adjustment against gender inequality indicators across countries and years.
queries: do austerity policies hurt women more

title: From Roe to Reagan: The Framing of Abortion in Congressional Hearings and the Development of Issue Positions
gloss: Traces how moral, feminist and medical framing of abortion in congressional hearings and presidential documents from Roe v. Wade (1973) through the Reagan administration built the partisan divide on abortion. Applies Carmines and Stimson's issue evolution model and Chong and Druckman's framing theory.
queries: how abortion became a partisan issue
history of party positions on abortion

title: “Americans aren’t serfs.” Institutional Investors, Nationalized Politics, and Congressional Housing Rhetoric
gloss: Asks whether House members whose districts have high institutional investor ownership of single-family homes talk more about housing in floor speeches, using 851 representative-Congress observations from the 117th and 118th Congresses plus four case studies. Bears on corporate landlords, housing affordability and nationalized politics.
queries: Wall Street buying single-family homes politics
do representatives talk about corporate landlords
Chloe Thurston political economy of housing

title: The Politics of Uncertainty: Information and the Making of Learned Political Helplessness in Lebanon
gloss: Asks why Lebanon's political system endures through economic collapse and repeated crises, arguing that a fragmented, politicized, crisis-normalizing information environment produces learned political helplessness that dampens collective action. Uses the October 2019 uprising as an exception, with content analysis, process tracing, interviews and an original national survey experiment.
queries: why Lebanese protests failed to change the system
why grievances don't lead to collective action

title: East Asian Pathways To Democracy Through External Democratizing Pressure: A Qualitative Comparative Analysis
gloss: Examines how external democratizing pressure interacts with domestic conditions to produce democratization or authoritarian resilience in fourteen East and Southeast Asian states from 1980 to 2000. Builds on Levitsky and Way's linkage and leverage framework using crisp-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis.
queries: why some East Asian countries democratized and others did not

title: Faith, Finance, & Political Change: Islamic Banking and Context-Dependent Development Across the Global South
gloss: Evaluates whether Islamic banking, built on Shari'ah principles such as the ban on interest (riba) and risk-sharing, actually delivers the inclusion, equality and stability its proponents claim across different political and institutional contexts in the Global South, including the Gulf states.
queries: ethical finance in the Global South

title: Why Did the 2014 and 2022 Sanctions Targeting Russian Oligarchs Fail to Achieve Their Intended Political Objectives?
gloss: Explains why Western sanctions on Russian oligarchs after the 2014 annexation of Crimea and the 2022 invasion of Ukraine failed to shift Kremlin policy, arguing they misread where leverage lies in a sultanistic oligarchy that depends on Putin. Draws on elite interviews with Western policymakers and analysts, documents and secondary literature.
queries: why sanctions on Russian oligarchs failed
Western response to the Ukraine invasion

title: Stay In Your Lane?: How Media Narratives Approximate Factional Demand in Presidential Primaries
gloss: Treats the lanes used to describe presidential primary fields as media-constructed categories and asks whether they reflect real voter preferences. Codes news coverage of the 2016 Republican and 2020 Democratic primaries and compares it with clustering of American National Election Studies survey data.
queries: do primary lanes reflect voter preferences

title: When Americans Are Taken: Comparing U.S. Responses to State and Non-State Hostage Takers
gloss: Compares how the US government responds when Americans are taken hostage by states (such as Iran, Russia or North Korea) versus non-state groups (such as terrorist organizations), using a small-N coded dataset, process-tracing case studies and a public opinion survey. Bears on hostage diplomacy, negotiation, concessions and coercion.
queries: how the US responds to Americans taken hostage
hostage diplomacy by states versus terrorist groups
should the US negotiate with hostage takers

title: To Nuke, or Not To Nuke: How Leaders’ Dispositions Influence Major Nuclear Decisions
gloss: Asks whether leaders' personality traits, specifically narcissism and self-esteem, shape decisions to acquire, test or use nuclear weapons. Compares Kim Jong-il, Harry Truman and Japan's Eisaku Sato through process tracing.
queries: do leaders' personalities affect nuclear decisions
Truman decision to drop the atomic bomb psychology
why Japan did not build nuclear weapons

title: The Role of Elite Cues and Endorsements of Political Violence in Shaping Individual Attitudes
gloss: Uses a survey experiment to test whether a Republican elite's rhetoric endorsing political violence changes Republicans' and Democrats' own support for political violence and their meta-perceptions of other partisans' support. Bears on partisan violence, dehumanization and elite cues.
queries: do politicians' violent words increase support for violence

title: Ideological Expectations: How Candidate Conservatism Shapes Voter Preferences for Women in U.S. Executive Elections
gloss: Asks whether conservatism helps women win executive office in the US, through content analysis scoring women governors' ideology since 1964 against their vote share and a vignette experiment on conservative versus less conservative female presidential candidates. Examines how perceived traditionalism and masculinity shape Democratic and Republican voters' responses.
queries: will the first woman president be a Republican
gender stereotypes and voting for women executives
women governors ideology and vote share

title: How does rights-based climate litigation impact environmental policy outcomes?: Evidence from Colombia and Nepal
gloss: Asks when lawsuits invoking a constitutional right to a healthy environment actually change climate and environmental policy, through process tracing of successful rights-based climate cases in Colombia and Nepal. Focuses on the specificity of court orders and civil society pressure.
concepts: Future Generations v. Ministry of Environment
Shrestha v. Office of the Prime Minister
queries: does climate litigation change government policy
right to a healthy environment courts
courts and climate action in the Global South

title: Recognition without Responsiveness: Comparing the Turkish-Armenian and Armenian-American Communities
gloss: Compares how Armenians in the United States and Turkey are classified by the state, and how those classifications shape their political voice, drawing on Brubaker, Hacking and Foucault. Based on interviews with Armenian Americans and with Turkish Armenians in Istanbul, it argues that both American multiculturalism and Turkish nationalism produce recognition without responsiveness.
queries: Elizabeth Shakman Hurd religion and minorities

title: A Troubling Refrain: The Impact of the Northern Irish Troubles on Far-Right Ideology in the Republic of Ireland
gloss: Asks whether the legacy of the Northern Irish Troubles contributed to the rise of far-right, anti-immigrant sentiment in the Republic of Ireland seen in the November 2023 Dublin riots. Based on interviews with Dublin City Councillors, it traces how Sinn Féin's moderation after the Good Friday Agreement left a working-class base open to far-right mobilization.
queries: rise of the far right in Ireland
legacy of the Troubles in Irish politics

title: Residents’ Right to the City in Barcelona, Venice, and Seoul
gloss: Compares residents' right to the city, in Henri Lefebvre's sense of residents' claim to shape and remain in urban space, in Barcelona, Venice and Seoul, likely in light of pressures such as mass tourism, gentrification and housing costs.
queries: right to the city comparative study
Lefebvre right to the city applied

title: Revisiting Mendelberg: Implicitness, Explicitness, and the Racial Politics of Messenger Identity
gloss: Revisits Tali Mendelberg's argument that the norm of racial equality pushes politicians toward implicit rather than explicit racial appeals, in an era of more open racial rhetoric. A preregistered survey experiment with white respondents varies rhetoric type and candidate race to see whether explicit appeals are sanctioned and how racial resentment moderates that.
queries: do explicit racial appeals still hurt candidates
Mendelberg implicit versus explicit race cues
Black versus white candidates using racial rhetoric

title: Framing the American Dream: Race, Merit, and Inequality in U.S. Billionaire Discourse
gloss: Analyzes how the 100 richest US billionaires explain inequality in their public interviews, speeches, shareholder letters and philanthropic communications, coding meritocratic versus structural accounts and color-evasive versus race-conscious framing. Asks how economic elites legitimate extreme wealth and the American Dream in a multiracial democracy.

title: Performative Activism on College Campuses: An Investigation into Efficacy
gloss: Asks whether performative activism on college campuses, such as social media posting and land acknowledgments, crowds out effective activism and how its drawbacks could be reduced. Uses survey experiments and interviews with students.

title: Justifying the Means: Explaining Generational Differences in Support for Political Violence
gloss: Explains why Generation Z Americans are more willing than older generations to justify political violence, a gap seen in polling after the 2025 killing of Charlie Kirk. An original survey experiment points to younger Americans' anti-establishment attitudes and, to a lesser degree, Democratic partisanship.
queries: why young Americans support political violence more
Gen Z attitudes toward political violence

title: Art and the Adversary: American Audience Perceptions of Russian Opera Amid the Russo-Ukrainian War
gloss: Tests how war-related priming and information about a performer's stance on Russia's invasion of Ukraine shape American audiences' perceptions of Russian opera, using a 2x3 factorial experiment with a clip of Anna Netrebko singing Tatyana's Letter Scene from Tchaikovsky's Eugene Onegin. Bears on cultural boycotts, soft power and programming decisions in wartime.
queries: should Russian artists be boycotted after the Ukraine invasion
cultural diplomacy and soft power in wartime
survey experiment on art and politics

title: Institutionalizing Inequality: Democracy and the Persistence of Wealth Inequality in Chile and Ecuador
gloss: Asks why democracy has not reduced wealth inequality in Latin America, comparing Chile's stable but highly unequal democracy with Ecuador's unstable one, both of which saw mass protests in October 2019. Process traces constitutional design, party systems, judicial independence and tax structures, contrasting an elite-biased democracy with a captured democracy.
queries: why democracy doesn't reduce inequality in Latin America

title: Beyond the Model Minority: Explaining Asian American Political Engagement Through Contact, Memory, and Civic Organizations
gloss: Examines when Asian Americans build coalitions with other racial minorities and achieve political incorporation, comparing Monterey Park, Oakland and Irvine. Combines precinct-level 2024 election analysis, archival research on responses to Black Lives Matter and Stop Asian Hate, and civic organization data to weigh intergroup contact, collective memory of discrimination and inclusive civic organizations.
queries: Asian American coalitions with Black and Latino voters
Stop Asian Hate and political mobilization
